name: Industry return of big firms
note: Not run. The signal cannot be built from daily prices and volume alone, and inventing a proxy would put a number in the ledger that does not measure what the paper measured.
error: needs firm size (shares outstanding / market cap) to split each industry into big and small firms; the panel carries prices only, and the signal is the big-firm leg predicting the small-firm leg, so the split is the signal rather than a detail

name: Intermediate Momentum
note: Re-test on free data 2005-2026, currently-listed names only, 10bp one-way costs. The paper reported t=5.79 over 1927–2010 on the full CRSP universe including delisted names. These are different samples, so this neither confirms nor refutes the published figure. It says whether the effect is visible today on data anyone can get.

name: Long-run reversal
note: Re-test on free data 2005-2026, currently-listed names only, 10bp one-way costs. The paper reported t=3.29 over 1929–1982 on the full CRSP universe including delisted names. These are different samples, so this neither confirms nor refutes the published figure. It says whether the effect is visible today on data anyone can get. Signal is sorted so the direction the paper predicts is the long leg: the raw variable is negated, so a positive spread here means the published effect shows up with the published sign.
